clauses.reason: Lead of Sec. 1: blocks property and interests in property of the persons described in items (a) to (c) that are in the United States or under United States control. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Covers persons who have contributed to the obstruction of implementation of UN Security Council Resolutions 841 and 873, the Governors Island Agreement of July 3, 1993, or the UN Mission in Haiti. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Covers persons who have perpetuated or contributed to violence in Haiti (item (b)) and persons who have materially or financially supported the foregoing (item (c)), and completes the blocking sentence. conflict_resolutions.FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT: The dossier flags that the sources read as both a whole and a partial ending for EO 12932. Resolution: EO 12932 revokes this order by number in a single sentence that names eight orders and also terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775, so it is a whole ending. Earlier partial provisions held for some of these orders (revocations to the extent inconsistent in later Haiti orders) are recorded as later events of the clauses they touch; each is conditional on inconsistency and none is shown to extinguish a clause, so none is an end.

research_rationale:
EO 12872 of October 18, 1993 (Blocking Property of Persons Obstructing Democratization in Haiti), read in full in the held Federal Register text (58 FR 54029, Federal Register of October 20, 1993; machine-extracted text layer with scan-spaced characters). Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row (1993-10-18). The order blocks property of persons who obstructed UN-backed democratization or supported violence in Haiti, bars evasion, authorizes Treasury regulations, and states its effective time. Inventory correction: the dossier inventory omits the Sec. 1 blocking lead and splits Sec. 5; I re-marked eight clauses on the held text. EO 12932 revokes the order by number effective 12:01 a.m. EDT October 16, 1994; the dossier's located-provision gaps (EO 12775, 12779, 12853, 12920, 12922) are orders held and read that do not revoke or amend this one. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning. Machine hits for this order: current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 10. The packet's by-number scan of held order texts (LOOKUPS) was read for this order; held texts citing this number are EO 12922 (which lists the order among those whose blocking provisions reach other persons) and EO 12932; no change provision other than EO 12932 was found.

savings.reason: EO 12932 states that the termination of the national emergency does not affect any action taken or proceeding pending, any action or proceeding based on an act committed before its effective date, or any rights or duties that matured or penalties incurred before it. Those preserved effects, and any Treasury regulations or licenses issued under the order, are accrued consequences or separate administrative acts; they are not commands of this order. No held source shows an independent standing command of this order after 1994-10-16.
